newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Legal blunder puts Irish government in the dock.
newsitem.headline: Legal blunder puts Irish government in the dock.

text.p: Ireland's two-year-old coalition government faces its first confidence vote on Tuesday amid opposition clamour over a blunder that gave temporary freedom to detainees on guerrilla charges.
But Prime Minister John Bruton, who heads a three-party administration, is confident of winning the vote, government officials said.

"I have no problem with the confidence vote. The government has worked very well and is continuing to work very well," Bruton told reporters after addressing an international conference on local development.
He said he had full confidence in Justice Minister Nora Owen, who is at the centre of the row, and said she had shown herself to be open and accountable in dealing with the matter.
Lawyers for 16 top-security prisoners freed and immediately recharged last week are expected on Tuesday to launch a High Court move to get them released.
They were briefly freed but rearrested within the grounds of the state's maximum security Portlaoise Prison after it was discovered they had been in illegal custody.
The judge who originally remanded them had not been told by the Justice Department that he was no longer a member of a three-judge anti-subversive "special criminal court".
Government officials described this as a "systems failure".
Opposition parties called it a startling gaffe by a government pledged to curb a domestic crime wave and crackdown on republican guerrilla groups waging war against British rule in Northern Ireland.

The bungle is being seen as a serious embarrassment for Bruton and his chief ministers, particularly Owen. They are engaged in intensive Anglo-Irish sponsored talks with Northern Ireland parties in Belfast.
Dick Spring, deputy prime minister and leader of the Labour Party, who will sum up in Tuesday's debate, said the government had moved quickly to set up an investigation into the affair.
"I said openly and honestly during the week that we have suffered a very serious embarrassment," he told Irish radio on Sunday.
